findings.summary: Spec §5 (lines 121-122) explicitly requires the dev-note's input_commit to equal the final delivery commit and warns the gate checks this item (citing the D1 incident). docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_g4a_question_wiring_01.md:5 records input_commit `bc8a30cb898c830e5e99d71f1f787233b36b5d8a`, but the continuous_review subject_commit / final delivery is `eac02b02d39827e9cf466a0592b8fa04805a59f3`. The actual subject commit appears in zero tracked evidence files (grep of `eac02b02...` returned no matches), while the dev-note's `bc8a30cb...` is a different commit entirely. This is the exact same Q8 evidence-integrity anti-pattern that rejected attempt 1 (where the note recorded `d375b8fa...` vs. subject `3917a167...`): the note stays at an earlier commit and the numbers do not match the deliverables. The functional wiring is correct and complete against §1/§2 (bin exports RESEARCH_QUESTION with no built-in default + loud failure at bin/deep-research-loop.sh:87-91; fleet.yaml.tpl:12 has research_question input; workflow.yaml:23 seeds the payload; tick.md:39-41 does incremental argv `tick_args+=(--question "$research_question")` per the §1.2 refactor; profiles/deploy/{production,local}.env add only the key with channel values unchanged; test/g4a-question-wiring.test.ts covers Q1-Q4 with Q2 as the reachability assertion via fake tick-entry argv logging, including the 8-case combination matrix at lines 168-205), but Q8 evidence integrity fails because the deliverable dev-note is stale relative to the subject commit.
